speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to begin our investigation, how long has your cough been persisting, and does it produce sputum?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Bronchitis.

The history of a productive cough lasting for at least three months over two consecutive years, combined with recurrent exacerbations requiring antibiotics, strongly supports a diagnosis of chronic bronchitis, despite the patient being a non-smoker.
